items.title: 56711_Buster Smith oral history interview
items.q: Well, I listened to the Fletcher Henderson and Duke Ellington bands.

ctx.x: Actually, this takes me back to the other thing about you, which is very interesting. Because you're a great arranger. How did you learn to do that? When did it start, and how and why? When did you get interested in it?

Well, I listened to the Fletcher Henderson and Duke Ellington bands. You listen to them... I know Fletcher was writing all the arrangements... I would get his records. I found out that he was... That the beautiful numbers, he had a technique going. He wrote some numbers that would sound so pretty, especially those ballad numbers, sweet numbers. He'd put them in a certain key to get that weird sound, and let Hawk take them solos. Like, he had "Talk Of The Town" -- he had in D-natural. See, a lot of fellows didn't…
